bug/question: prefetch data into client components in libs

Verify canary release I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release Provide environment information [code omitted] Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure) App directory (appDir: true) Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug [link] To Reproduce [code omitted] See infinite rerenders: [link] Describe the Bug Consider libs targeting the app directory, or just "the new React" in general. They export some component. This component is interactive, so it needs to be a client component. But it also uses data from the server, so it fetches that, preferably using `<Suspense>` to avoid flickering loading states. The solution we're advised to take in our apps is to fetch the data in a Server Component, then pass it to the client component as props. This doesn't really work in lib-land since bundlers often doesn't handle the `"use client"` directive "properly" to deal with the client component to be nested in the server component. Therefore, it would be much easier for this data to be fetched directly from the client component. The problem then becomes, how do we do that and still trigger the Suspense boundary? `use` sounds like a good shout, but we can't `fetch` in `use` (yet) without causing infinite rerenders. I know React Query can handle `Suspense`, but do we need a third-party data fetching library to handle the suspense for us, just to get a tiny bit of data prerendered in our component? I don't really wanna have all that logic in my lib. I have previously managed to get around this by storing the promise in a ref and `use`-ing the ref instead of the fetch call directly: [code omitted] However, this doesn't seem to work anymore. So, how should library authors handle this? Expected Behavior My client component should be able to fetch some data and using Suspense. Which browser are you using? One such example of this is `node-fetch`, which can be seen in the compiled section of the next.js npm tarball. `node-fetch` _generally works._ However, in our project, we have 10s of teams issues 1000s of queries. With that volume, probabilistically, we start hitting all of the edge cases. `node-fetch` has many open issues ([link] some quite fatal 1 2. By using package manager solutions (overrides, resolutions, hooks, etc), we were able to circumvent flaws in transitive dependencies easily before, to use versions and patches to workaround issues of interest gracefully. However, precompiling such dependencies in the distribution makes correcting such issues ergonomically challenging. Next.js ejects from traditional dependency distribution, and even meddles with node internals (module resolution), hindering me from using a specific version of node-fetch that I require in the active node process, both within a next.js context & within my custom server. Possible solutions: 1. Fix the upstream bugs, then upgrade next.js to use the latest upstream versions. This is the ideal outcome, always. However, in a world of perpetual change, it's not the most tenable. Bugs will always exist, and consuming projects will always lag behind. 1. Use patch-package! Spec bug: HTTP’s 400 Bad Request shouldn’t map to gRPC’s INTERNAL

The HTTP docs say that a 400 Bad Request error is the client’s fault: > The 400 (Bad Request) status code indicates that the server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing). The gRPC docs say a INTERNAL error is the server’s fault: > Internal errors. This means that some invariants expected by the underlying system have been broken. This error code is reserved for serious errors. But the status mapping doc maps 400 to INTERNAL: | HTTP Status Code | gRPC Status Code | | -- | -- | | 400 Bad Request | INTERNAL | | 401 Unauthorized | UNAUTHENTICATED | | 403 Forbidden | PERMISSION_DENIED | | 404 Not Found | UNIMPLEMENTED | | 429 Too Many Requests | UNAVAILABLE | | 502 Bad Gateway | UNAVAILABLE | | 503 Service Unavailable | UNAVAILABLE | | 504 Gateway Timeout | UNAVAILABLE | | All other codes | UNKNOWN | I think this is a spec bug! The spec should instead map HTTP 400s to INVALID_ARGUMENT, which is the status code that best-fits ‘client’s fault’: > The client specified an invalid argument. Note that this differs from FAILED_PRECONDITION. INVALID_ARGUMENT indicates arguments that are problematic regardless of the state of the system (e.g., a malformed file name). Why do I care? When an error occurs it’s very nice to correctly attribute blame to the client or the server. If it’s the client’s fault and the server engineers get paged, then the wrong people are awaken in the middle of the night. That is an inconvenience to the server owners who have to triage a bug, and to the client owners who have to wait for the server team to tell them they can fix their own problem. And it delays mitigation of the problem. See also [link]

[Feature request] zero_increase to easily compute increase in new counters

Proposal `increase` does report 0 for counters that are created during the time window, whatever their first value is. It's how it's designed and it's not a bug. However, it would be nice to have an alternative to `increase`, like `zero_increase`, that uses zero when the counter doesn't exist yet, so you could compute an increase from zero when a new counter is created. An example is a metric with an error code as a label. For a given error code, it doesn't exist until the first error occurs. *Unless you initialize all your metrics with all possible labels of course.* `increase` will return 0 even if the first value of the counter is higher than zero. If errors with the same label do not occur again in following time windows, you could notice that a new error code label is there, but the line chart would only show zero errors for it. If you want to see a spike in the chart when the error happens, you cannot use `increase` and have to rely on complex queries. `zero_increase` would easily offer this feature. It's related to #1673, which has been locked by a bot.

Add Host Binding Feature to Prometheus Emitter

Proposal Summary The Prometheus emitter cannot currently bind to a specific host. This feature is crucial for environments where binding to all interfaces (default behaviour) is not desired or poses security concerns. This ticket aims to enhance the Prometheus emitter by introducing a configurable host binding option. Details Problem Statement: Currently, the Prometheus emitter binds to all available network interfaces. This behaviour might not be ideal in certain deployment scenarios, especially in multi-homed environments or where strict network security policies are enforced. Proposed Solution: - Implement a configuration option specifying a particular host/IP address to which the Prometheus emitter should bind. This option should be flexible enough to support different deployment needs (e.g., binding to localhost for local monitoring, binding to a specific interface in multi-homed setups). - Expected Outcome: Once implemented, users can configure the Prometheus emitter to bind to a specific host/IP. This enhancement will provide better security and more control over network traffic management. Use Cases: Bind to `localhost` for scenarios where Prometheus metrics are only consumed locally. Specify a particular network interface in environments with multiple network interfaces to control network exposure. Implementation Notes: A new configuration parameter (e.g., `hostBindAddress`) should be introduced. The emitter's network binding logic should be updated to respect this new parameter, defaulting to the current behaviour (binding to all interfaces) when not specified. Security: Reduced attack surface by preventing the Prometheus emitter from exposing metrics on all network interfaces. Flexibility: Users gain more control over their Prometheus emitter deployments, tailoring them to specific network requirements.

Feature Request: Visual Line Mode (Inspired by Emacs)

Problem Is your feature request related to a problem? When working with long lines that are wrapped to fit the window, Neovim's default line-wise motion commands `(j, k, ^, $)` treat the wrapped parts as a single continuous line. This makes navigation cumbersome and inefficient. For instance, pressing j moves the cursor to the start of the next logical line, not the next visual line on the screen. This is a significant friction point for users who often work with wrapped text, such as markdown, documentation, or code with long comments. Expected behavior I propose adding a new mode, similar to Emacs' "visual line mode," that treats wrapped lines as distinct, navigable lines. This feature is documented here. In this mode, the following behaviours would be implemented: Vertical Motion: j and k would move the cursor up and down by one visual line on the screen, not one logical line. This would allow users to navigate the wrapped text as it's displayed. Horizontal Motion: ^ and $ would move the cursor to the beginning and end of the visual line, respectively. This would be a toggle-able option, similar to set wrap, so users could enable it as needed.

Integrate Polaris go sdk to support their service governance ability.

本 Proposal 目的是制定一种异常规范用于区分 RPC 异常和用户自定义的异常。我们希望将 RPC 错误和业务的错误能够区分开，RPC 错误表示一次RPC 请求失败，比如超时、熔断、限流，从 RPC 层面是失败的请求，但业务错误属于业务逻辑层面，在 RPC 层面其实是请求成功。服务监控建议对于 RPC 错误上报为请求失败，而业务层面错误，上报为请求成功，但上报 status_code 用于识别错误码。该能力对于工程实践具有一定的价值。 BizError 接口定义 内置 BizStatusErrorIface 提供用户实现自定义异常接口，框架同时提供默认实现，用户也可以自定义实现，比如 gRPC 用户自定义的 Error 可同时实现 `interface{ GRPCStatus() *status.Status }`，可以复用 Status 的 Detail 用于透传更丰富的业务信息。 [code omitted] 用户使用 [code omitted] 框架实现 依赖传输协议透传自定义异常的错误码和错误信息，Thrift 和 Kitex Protobuf 依赖 TTHeader，Kitex gRPC 依赖HTTP2。 - Thrift：使用 TTHeader - Kitex Protobuf：使用 TTHeader - gRPC：使用 HTTP2 Header | 优点 | 缺点 | | :----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 对用户来说 Thrift/Protobuf 使用方式统一，不需要修改idl | 1. 框架层面异常处理有些分裂：框架异常通过Payload中的错误信息传递；用户自定义异常通过header传递；2. 裸Thrift无法支持，用户必须指定 TTHeader | 框架处理 TTHeader 新增三个string key，分别是 biz-status 、 biz-message 和 biz-extra。 对于服务端，如果用户通过 NewBizStatusError 构造了 error，将 errorCode 、 message 和 extra信息 分别装填到biz-status、biz-message 和 biz-extra； 对于调用端，如果 TTHeader 中 biz-status != 0，则构造 BizStatusError 返回给用户。 Streaming - gRPC gRPC 的异常信息是通过 Header传递的，errorCode 和 message 分别对应 header 中的 grpc-status 和 grpc-message。框架处理时只需将 errorCode 和 errorMsg 装填到 header 中即可。 但 gRPC 定义的 Status Error 也未区分框架异常和用户自定义异常，grpc-status 作为框架对异常类型的识别，Kitex 增加错误码约束， grpc-status=10000 表示用户异常，message 复用 grpc-message，因为用户异常和框架异常不会同时出现。

Proposal: Kitex support xDS Protocol

背景 希望 Kitex 能够原生支持 xDS 协议 ，让 Kitex 服务能够以 Proxyless 的模式被服务网格统一纳管，从而丰富网格数据面部署架构形态，让用户可以在不同场景下有更多更适合特定场景的部署形态选择 目标 - 完成 Kitex 对接 xDS 之后整体架构形态设计 - 完成 Kitex 框架治理能力如何适配 xDS 模型的概要设计 设计介绍 整体架构 整体主要有几个模块组成： - Control Plane：控制面，负责管理数据面并基于 xDS 协议下发治理规则 - Kitex Application：Kitex 内部整体主要分为两层 - xDS 层： - xDS Client：封装基于 xDS 协议与控制面交互逻辑 - xDS Resource Manger：管理 xDS 各协议资源的缓存，并对外提供发布订阅能力 - 治理能力层：基于框架提供的治理能力拓展机制，来适配 xDS 模型，实现各种数据面治理能力 框架治理能力适配 为了对接治理能力，框架需要做的适配包括以下几部分： 添加 `RouterMW`，顺序在内置中间件的第一位（动态路由后才能确定之后的配置）。 扩展 `Resolver` 接口实现 `XdsResolver`，判断服务发现类型，基于 eds 获取实例信息。 扩展 `LoadBalancer` 接口实现 `XdsLoadbalancer`，根据 cds 动态调整负载均衡策略。 各种治理能力适配思路如下 1. 服务注册 Istio 虽然本身不提供服务注册中心，但是内部维护了统一的服务模型和服务注册表，并且支持集成两种类型的服务注册中心 Provider - Kubernetes：基于 K8S APIServer List-Watch ，注册并发现 Kubernetes 上的服务 - External：注册并发现外部服务，其中外部服务以 ServiceEntries 的形式定义，可以直接 ServiceEntry CRD 描述，也可以通过 MCP-over-xDS 的方式，以外部数据源的方式注册进来 因此，我们在该方案中无需去设计并实现一套服务注册流程了，只需要直接去对接现有的服务注册中心即可。 2. 动态路由 流程大致如下所示： 1. 增加一个 xDS Router MW 来负责 Pick Cluster（路由），watch 目标服务的 LDS 及 RDS 2. 感知 LDS 变化，并提取目标服务的 LDS 中的 Filter Chain 及其 inline RDS 3. 感知 RDS 变化，根据 VirtualHost 和 ServiceName 来匹配（支持前缀、后缀、精确、通配），获取目标服务的路由配置 4. 遍历处理匹配到的 RDS 中的路由规则，路由规则主要分为两部分（参考：路由规范定义）： 1. Match（支持前缀、后缀、精确、通配等），目前版本我们支持以下两种即可： 1. Path（必须项）：从 rpcinfo 提取 Method进行匹配 2. HeaderMatcher（可选项）：可自定义需要匹配的元数据，比如 metainfo 内的 key-value。 2. Route： 1. Cluster：标准 Cluster 2. WeightedClusters（权重路由）：MW 内根据权重来选择 cluster 3. 将选择到的 Cluster 写入 EndpointInfo.Tag，用于之后的服务发现。 3. 服务发现 基于 Kitex 的 Resolver 接口，拓展一个 XDSResolver 来进行服务发现。 - 根据 RDS 找到对应的 CDS （Pick Cluster）之后，进入 Resolve 阶段，通过根据 CDS 获取对应的 Cluster 配置，包括负载均衡策略、熔断等。之后拉取 EDS 资源以获取实例信息，并根据对应的 LB 策略，pick 出最终的一个 Endpoint。 服务发现类型包括以下几种： - Static：直接返回实例的地址 - Static DNS：数据面需要执行 DNS 解析，以获得所有的实例信息。（异步、周期性地解析） - Logical DNS：执行 DNS 解析，只有当需要建立连接时才使用返回实例信息中的第一个。static DNS 的返回结果是完整的实例信息，当两次的结果不同，则需要清理连接。而 logic DNS 则会维持连接，直至被回收。 - EDS：与控制面交互，发送 eds 请求，以获得实例信息。 4. 负载均衡 Lb policy 包含在 CDS 内，所以 lb 策略的变化是在动态路由选定 cluster 之后获取并应用的。 Kitex 支持自定义 LoadBalancer，实际上就是根据lb策略，从服务发现获得的实例列表

Making "for update" configurable in beforeImage stage.

Why you need it? 当执行update或delete语句时，beforeImage肯定会给select语句加"for update"限制，以保证数据不被脏写或者脏读。但是这会加重数据库的负担，因为我们不能要求所有的人都对表建立好了完美的索引。因此一旦执行select for update语句，就会有可能产生锁表的行为。在大流量并发时，完全有可能导致出现多个表死锁。如果业务中断，这是不被接受的。 Seata will append "for update" to select statement in beforeImage method If we execute update or delete SQL. This action will protect our data from dirty reads and dirty write. But this will give a lot of pressure to the database. Because we can't ask everyone to build a perfect index for their database. So it may cause table locking if we execute "select for update" SQL. Furthermore, Multiple tables will lock when we encounter massive traffic. It is not acceptable to crash a website for this reason. How it could be? 能否增加一个配置项，让开发者能根据自己的情况配置是否在beforeImage阶段进行for update。比起让网站宕机，我更能够接受脏读或者脏写。 Can you make "for update" configurable? Let developers decide if "select for update" in beforeImage stage by their own situation. I can accept dirty reads or dirty writes more than taking my website down.
